description: The Global Carbon Project's projection of carbon dioxide emissions from fossil fuels and industry in 2025, made from data for part of the year: 38.1 billion tonnes, 1.0 percent more than in 2024 (range 0.2 to 1.7 percent). It is net of the carbon dioxide that cement takes back up as it ages (the cement carbonation sink), like the paper's headline value for 2024.

processing.description: Quoted from Executive summary, p. 3215. The quote was found in the text of page 5 of the snapshot (sha256 166e10a66b4d…) before publishing.
Value: "38.1 GtCO₂ yr⁻¹" is published as 38.1 billion tonnes of carbon dioxide per year in 2025, the paper's own value in carbon dioxide units (not converted by us from the 10.4 GtC it also states).

published_value.quote: Global fossil CO₂ emissions (including cement carbonation) are expected to further increase in 2025 by 1.0 % relative to 2024 (range 0.2 % to 1.7 %), bringing fossil emissions to an expected 10.4 GtC yr⁻¹ (38.1 GtCO₂ yr⁻¹).

scope.basis: Fossil fuels and industry including the cement carbonation sink (net), with international aviation and shipping. A projection from preliminary data for 2025, published in May 2026; the final 2025 value comes with the Global Carbon Budget 2026.

title: Fossil carbon dioxide emissions projected for 2025 (Global Carbon Budget)

unit.label: billion tonnes of carbon dioxide per year
